summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of idiopathic intracranial hypertension and migraines was admitted for intractable headaches. Her lumbar puncture revealed an elevated opening pressure of 30 cm H2O, leading to the decision for ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, which was performed successfully on 2140-09-17. During the hospitalization, her migraine prophylaxis was optimized with increased valproic acid and restart of amitriptyline, and her diabetes management was intensified with the addition of Lantus insulin. She showed clinical improvement post-shunt, with reduced headache severity, and was discharged home with close neurology follow-up and updated medication instructions.
